chosen.premise: Blastoise can accurately hit an empty can from more than 160 feet away with a water bullet.
chosen.hook: Blastoise can snipe a can from over 160 feet away.
chosen.visualIdea: A tiny can sits 160+ feet away; targeting reticle locks on and a water shot nails it.
chosen.note: The precise distance, tiny target, and water-bullet premise create an immediately understandable challenge. It is directly supported by two Pokédex entries and is exceptionally easy to visualize.

candidates.premise: Blastoise deliberately makes itself heavy so its own water-cannon recoil will not launch it backward.
candidates.hook: Blastoise makes itself heavier on purpose.
candidates.visualIdea: Blastoise lowers its stance as a weight meter rises, then absorbs cannon recoil without moving.
candidates.note: A genuinely distinctive contradiction: Blastoise intentionally becomes heavy to counter its own recoil. The mechanic is excellent, though the visual requires explaining an unseen physiological choice.

candidates.premise: Blastoise’s shell cannons fire water jets powerful enough to punch holes through thick steel.
candidates.hook: Blastoise doesn’t just spray water—it can punch through steel.
candidates.visualIdea: A Blastoise cannon blast hits a thick steel plate, then a clean hole appears through it.
candidates.note: Strong, unmistakably Blastoise, and directly supported by multiple Pokédex entries. “Thick steel” is dramatic but visually and narratively vague compared with the distance feat.

candidates.premise: At 1.6 meters and 85.5 kg normally, Blastoise’s Gmax form becomes 25 meters tall and 1,000 kg.
candidates.hook: Blastoise can grow from 1.6 meters to 25 meters tall.
candidates.visualIdea: A normal Blastoise stands beside a scale, then rapidly expands into its 25-meter Gmax silhouette.
candidates.note: The transformation has excellent numbers and visual scale, but size-growth comparisons work for many Dynamax or Gmax Pokémon, making it less uniquely Blastoise.

candidates.premise: Blastoise uses pressurized shell jets not only to shoot, but to power high-speed tackles.
candidates.hook: Blastoise uses its cannons like rocket boosters.
candidates.visualIdea: Shell jets ignite behind Blastoise, turning a standing turtle into a high-speed charging impact.
candidates.note: The high-speed-tackle fact supports the idea, and the action is highly visual. “Rocket boosters” is an effective analogy rather than wording directly established by the research.

candidates.premise: Once Blastoise aims, its water blast hits with even more force than a fire hose.
candidates.hook: A fire hose is weaker than Blastoise after it locks on.
candidates.visualIdea: Split screen: a fire hose blasts one target, then Blastoise’s aimed cannon overwhelms the other.
candidates.note: The comparison is accessible and punchy, but it relies on one entry and “more force than a fire hose” lacks a measurable benchmark. The split-screen visual could also overstate the claim.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required; the selected angle already combines the best specificity, surprise, visual clarity, and direct support. A stronger alternative would need an equally precise feat that is even more uniquely Blastoise.
